topic.title: Five open mass-spec libraries as public S3 mirrors, plus a notebook that joins them
topic.forumName: Enveda CASMI 2026 - Molecule ID From Mass Spectra
topic.content:
External data disclosure, per the host's pinned post. These are all open-licence, free to everyone, and mirrored byte for byte with md5 manifests.

Public S3, no account needed:

Enveda-180 (Zenodo 20436851, CC BY 4.0): 1,158,293 timsTOF MS/MS spectra for 184,330 Enamine compounds, with CCS and RT. s3://scigantic-zenodo-20436851/

COCONUT 2.0, October 2026 (CC0): 738,794 natural-product structures with organisms and NPClassifier classes, as Parquet. s3://scigantic-coconut/coconut-10-2026.parquet

LOTUS (CC BY 4.0): 674,454 structure, organism, reference triples. s3://scigantic-zenodo-19360665/

MassBank 2026.03, open-licence records only (NC records excluded): 96,949 reference spectra of 10,304 compounds, as MSP and Parquet. s3://scigantic-massbank/massbank_open_spectra.parquet

GNPS community libraries (CC0): 581,722 spectra from 65 directly contributed libraries, as MGF and Parquet. s3://scigantic-gnps-libraries/gnps_community_spectra.parquet

Every bucket has a MIRROR.md at its root with the source, licence and per-file md5. Cite the upstream resource, not the mirror.

A notebook that follows one natural product (quercetin) through all five, then measures how little of Enveda-180 overlaps natural-product chemical space, runs in the browser with the files already mounted (free account): https://scigantic.com/archive/55cedfbf-558a-5d74-9e95-440df1dc72d6/sample

Two things we measured that matter for the hidden test: Enveda-180 is Enamine screening compounds, so a plant isolate almost never has a library match there, only chemical neighbours; and 2,077 Enveda-180 compounds also have a positive-mode [M+H]+ spectrum in GNPS, which is a usable cross-instrument check.

We mirrored these for our own entry (team scigantic). Disclosed here so they are equally available to everyone.
